priorities.finding: Prioritize request-context features tab, hour, and weekday. Training-only screening shows positive primary lift of 0.00221 on all four days, with full coverage; the lift is directionally consistent but small relative to daily variability. Official validation shows GAUC 0.6689 and nDCG@5 0.5370, supporting a cautious confirmatory follow-up rather than immediate broad expansion.
priorities.recommended_action: Continue only with a bounded confirmation using the same leakage-safe features and unchanged model budget. Early-stop if the next temporal holdout does not preserve positive within-user ranking lift.

priorities.finding: Prioritize diagnosis of tab-specific failures. Tab 8 has a genuine within-user ranking weakness with GAUC 0.3519 and primary 0.1891; tabs 3 and 0 also have GAUC near or below 0.50 and materially negative primary deltas. These are not merely top-five weaknesses.
priorities.recommended_action: Audit candidate availability, label prevalence, and request-context distributions for these tabs before spending budget on new features; consider targeted fallback or separate treatment only after confirming sufficient sample stability.

priorities.finding: The user-positive-count diagnostic is dominated by retrospective label composition. The zero-positive segment has GAUC 0.50 and zero top-five metrics because it contains no positives, while users with one or more positives show substantially stronger top-five performance. This should not be interpreted as evidence of a feature-ranking failure.
priorities.recommended_action: Do not optimize features against the zero-positive slice. Track it as a coverage and evaluation-population issue, and use GAUC plus positive-bearing-user slices for ranking decisions.
